title: Support split_group on the fake process group backend
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #186290

The "fake" backend (FakeProcessGroup) did not support split_group: the
Python API raised "backend does not support splitting" before doing any
work, and the C++ path was missing several pieces split_group needs.
new_group works on fake because it re-invokes the backend creator and only
seeds sequence numbers for gloo/nccl; split_group instead drives the generic
ProcessGroup::splitGroup machinery, which exercises code paths the fake
backend never implemented.

Reviewing in dependency order:

- FakeProcessGroup gains supportsSplitting() and a split() that returns a
  child FakeProcessGroup whose rank is the position of this rank within the
  sorted subgroup (mirroring ProcessGroupNCCL::split), or nullptr when this
  rank is not a member.
- setSequenceNumberForGroup()/getSequenceNumberForGroup() are overridden as
  no-ops; split_group unconditionally seeds a sequence number on the child,
  whereas the base Backend implementation throws.
- The FakeProcessGroup constructor coalesces a null Options to a fresh one.
  init_process_group passes pg_options=None to the creator, so the default
  fake PG had a null options_; ProcessGroup::splitGroup dereferences
  getBackendOptions() and would otherwise crash.
- FakeProcessGroup.Options gains __copy__/__deepcopy__, since split_group
  does copy.deepcopy(parent_backend.options).
- FakeStore is reimplemented in C++ (FakeStore.hpp) as a no-op store and
  re-exported from torch.testing._internal.distributed.fake_pg. split_group
  clones the parent store, and the process group holds the store only at the
  C++ level; a pure-Python Store.clone() override is garbage collected once
  the caller drops its reference, so clone() must be a real C++ method.

For the store, subclassing HashStore (which has a real clone()) and stubbing
the methods in Python were both considered. The former turns the fake store
into a functional KV store; the latter does not fix clone()'s lifetime
problem. A dedicated C++ no-op store avoids both issues.

Test Plan:

```
python -m pytest test/distributed/test_fake_pg.py -q
```

New tests cover split rank assignment (an interleaved, unsorted split so the
child rank cannot coincide with the parent rank, cross-checked with
get_global_rank), non-member ranks returning None, and split working when the
caller does not retain the store. Also ran the other fake-store users:

```
python -m pytest test/distributed/test_device_mesh.py -q -k fake_pg
python -m pytest test/distributed/test_collective_utils.py -q
```

Authored by Claude.
